Sample-selection correction for linear panel models

Source: R/panselect.R
panselect.Rd

Two-step selection correction of Wooldridge (1995) for linear panel models in which the outcome is observed only for a selected subsample (attrition in a cohort, survival, response to a wave), when selection may depend on the idiosyncratic error of the outcome equation.

Usage

panselect(
  selection,
  outcome,
  data,
  index,
  model = c("within", "pooling"),
  mundlak = TRUE,
  lambda = c("period", "common"),
  boot = 199L,
  seed = NULL,
  na.action = stats::na.omit
)

Arguments

selection

a two-sided formula s ~ z1 + x1 + ... for the selection equation; s is a 0/1 (or logical) indicator equal to one when the outcome is observed

outcome

a two-sided formula y ~ x1 + ... for the outcome equation, fitted on the observations with s == 1

data

a data.frame in long format, with one row per individual and period whether or not the outcome is observed

index

length-2 character vector giving the individual and period columns

model

"within" (fixed effects in the outcome equation) or "pooling" (pooled OLS, with Mundlak means when mundlak = TRUE)

mundlak

logical; add the individual means of the time-varying selection regressors to the probits (and to the pooled outcome equation)

lambda

"period" (inverse Mills ratio interacted with period dummies) or "common" (a single inverse Mills ratio term)

boot

number of panel bootstrap replicates; 0 skips the bootstrap and makes the cluster-robust covariance the default

seed

optional random seed for the bootstrap; the global random number state is restored afterwards

na.action

missing-data action passed to stats::model.frame() for each formula

Value

an object of class "panselect", a list with components coefficients, vcov (the default covariance), vcov_type ("boot" or "cluster"), vcov_boot, vcov_cluster, vcov_classical, boot (the replicate estimates, the number of requested and failed replicates), probit (a list with the probit coefficients of each period, NULL for a period without probit), lambda_terms (names of the correction terms), selection_test (the cluster-robust and bootstrap Wald tests), imr (the inverse Mills ratio of every observation of the selection sample, in the row order of the data), residuals, nobs (selected observations used), nobs_selection, n_groups, n_groups_selection, df.residual, periods, model, mundlak, lambda, call. Methods: print, summary, coef, vcov, confint, predict, nobs, tidy and glance.

Estimator

Step 1. For each period t a probit of the selection indicator s_it on the selection regressors z_it and, with mundlak = TRUE, the individual means zbar_i of the time-varying selection regressors (the Mundlak version of Chamberlain's device) is fitted on all observations of that period (by iteratively reweighted least squares, as stats::glm(), with the convergence tolerance 1e-12). The inverse Mills ratio is lambda_it = dnorm(xb_it) / pnorm(xb_it) with xb_it the probit index. The means are taken over all observations of the individual in the selection sample, selected or not. A period in which every observation (or none) is selected has no probit; its inverse Mills ratio is set to zero and it gets no correction term (for instance the first wave of a cohort, before any attrition).

Step 2. The outcome equation is fitted on the selected observations, adding the inverse Mills ratio interacted with period dummies, lambda_it * d_t (lambda = "period", Wooldridge's specification, one coefficient per period with a probit) or a single term lambda_it (lambda = "common"). With model = "within" the individual effects are removed by the within transformation on the selected sample; with model = "pooling" the outcome equation is estimated by pooled OLS and, when mundlak = TRUE, includes the same Mundlak means zbar_i to account for the correlation between the individual effect and the regressors. Period effects are not added automatically; include them in outcome (e.g. + factor(wave)) when needed.

The selection regressors should contain the outcome regressors plus at least one excluded variable (an instrument that affects selection but not the outcome); without one the correction is identified only by the nonlinearity of the inverse Mills ratio, and a warning is given.

Inference

The coefficient standard errors default to a panel (cluster) bootstrap: whole individuals are resampled with replacement and both steps, including the Mundlak means and the per-period probits, are re-estimated in each replicate. The covariance is the sample covariance of the boot replicate estimates; replicates that fail are dropped and counted.

The cluster-robust covariance vcov(fit, type = "cluster") treats the inverse Mills ratios as known regressors. It ignores the estimation of the first step and is therefore not valid for the coefficients when there is selection bias. It uses the factor G / (G - 1) * (n - 1) / (n - k), as in plm::vcovHC(type = "sss").

The test of selection bias is the joint Wald test that all inverse Mills ratio coefficients are zero. Under this null hypothesis the first step does not affect the asymptotic distribution of the second-step estimator, so the cluster-robust Wald statistic is valid (Wooldridge 2010, section 19.9); it is chi-squared with as many degrees of freedom as correction terms. The same statistic computed with the bootstrap covariance is reported as well.

Validation

No R package implements this panel estimator, so the package's validation suite on GitHub checks it step by step: the period probits against stats::glm(), the second step against plm::plm() and stats::lm() with cluster covariances from plm::vcovHC() and sandwich::vcovCL(), the one-period case against the two-step sampleSelection::heckit() on the Mroz (1987) data, and the recovery of the true coefficients in simulations with selection on the idiosyncratic error.

References

Wooldridge, J. M. (1995). Selection corrections for panel data models under conditional mean independence assumptions. Journal of Econometrics, 68, 115-132.

Wooldridge, J. M. (2010). Econometric Analysis of Cross Section and Panel Data, 2nd edition, section 19.9. MIT Press.

See also

summary.panselect(), vcov.panselect() and predict.panselect() for the fitted model, tidy-methods for tidy() and glance().

Other panel models: panfmm(), panfmmselect(), panglm(), pangmm(), panhurdle(), paniv(), panqr(), twopart()

Examples

# Simulated cohort of 300 patients followed over 4 waves. A quality of
# life score is observed only for patients who answer the questionnaire;
# non-response depends on the same health shock that lowers the score,
# and on a reminder letter that does not affect the score itself.
set.seed(1)
N <- 300; TT <- 4
d <- data.frame(id = rep(seq_len(N), each = TT), wave = rep(seq_len(TT), N))
alpha <- rep(rnorm(N), each = TT)
d$treat <- rnorm(N * TT) + 0.5 * alpha
d$reminder <- rnorm(N * TT)
v <- rnorm(N * TT)
u <- 0.7 * v + rnorm(N * TT, sd = 0.7)
d$respond <- as.numeric(0.3 + 0.5 * d$treat + d$reminder + 0.3 * alpha + v > 0)
d$qol <- ifelse(d$respond == 1, 1 + 0.5 * d$treat + alpha + u, NA)

fit <- panselect(respond ~ treat + reminder, qol ~ treat, data = d,
                 index = c("id", "wave"), model = "within", boot = 49, seed = 2)
summary(fit)
#> 
#> Call:
#> panselect(selection = respond ~ treat + reminder, outcome = qol ~ 
#>     treat, data = d, index = c("id", "wave"), model = "within", 
#>     boot = 49, seed = 2)
#> 
#> Wooldridge (1995) panel selection correction: fixed effects with Mundlak means, inverse Mills ratio by period 
#> Selection sample: N = 1200  groups = 300 
#> Outcome sample:   N = 710  groups = 286 
#> Probits fitted for periods: 1, 2, 3, 4 
#> 
#> Outcome equation (vcov: panel bootstrap, 49 replicates):
#>          Estimate Std. Error z value Pr(>|z|)    
#> treat     0.45225    0.05037   8.978  < 2e-16 ***
#> lambda:1  0.98046    0.18266   5.368 7.98e-08 ***
#> lambda:2  0.76097    0.17850   4.263 2.02e-05 ***
#> lambda:3  0.80668    0.21728   3.713 0.000205 ***
#> lambda:4  0.81105    0.17365   4.671 3.00e-06 ***
#> ---
#> Signif. codes:  0 ‘***’ 0.001 ‘**’ 0.01 ‘*’ 0.05 ‘.’ 0.1 ‘ ’ 1
#>
